subquestions.label: a
subquestions.text: Identify the main entities and their attributes.

subquestions.label: b
subquestions.text: Draw the ER/EER diagram showing relationships and cardinalities.

questions.text: Consider the following relation schema: Flight(FlightID, Airline, DepartureCity, ArrivalCity, DepartureTime, ArrivalTime). The functional dependencies are given by F = {FlightID → Airline, DepartureCity, ArrivalCity, DepartureTime, ArrivalTime; Airline, DepartureCity → ArrivalCity, DepartureTime, ArrivalTime}. Analyze this relation and its dependencies for normalization purposes.

subquestions.label: a
subquestions.text: Draw the functional dependency diagram for the relation Flight.

subquestions.label: b
subquestions.text: Use the attribute closure and identify the primary key for the relation Flight.

subquestions.label: c
subquestions.text: If we insert a row <FL123, Delta, Atlanta, New York, 10:00, 12:00> into the relation, what is the update anomaly that is violated? Give reasons.

subquestions.label: d
subquestions.text: Assume that the relation has a row <FL456, Southwest, Miami, Los Angeles, 15:00, 17:30>. If we remove the flight FL456, what is the possible update anomaly that can be violated? Give reasons.

subquestions.label: e
subquestions.text: Using the above functional dependencies, design a set of 3NF relations for the relation Flight. Show clearly each stage in deriving the 3NF relations. Also identify the normal form at each of these stages.

subquestions.label: f
subquestions.text: Do the update anomalies of part (c) and (d) hold in the 3NF relations? Discuss briefly.

subquestions.label: g
subquestions.text: Are the 3NF relations derived in part (e) still in 3NF? Justify your answer.

subquestions.label: h
subquestions.text: Are the 3NF relations derived in part (e) in BCNF? If not, bring the relations to BCNF.
